stem: Which service model gives a customer control over a VM guest OS?

explanations.A: That is a deployment model rather than this responsibility boundary.
explanations.B: Infrastructure services expose guest operating-system control.
explanations.C: Finished software normally hides its OS.
explanations.D: Managed platforms operate the underlying OS.

stem: Who normally maintains an IaaS guest application?

explanations.A: Manufacturing does not maintain application logic.
explanations.C: Visitors do not administer the app.
explanations.D: The customer operates its code on the infrastructure.

stem: A legacy app requires OS-level customization. Which model deserves evaluation?

choices.C: A managed platform with no OS access

explanations.A: Offline data storage is not application compute.
explanations.B: A finished email service does not host this legacy app.
explanations.C: That cannot satisfy the stated customization.
explanations.D: VM control can meet guest OS requirements.

stem: Which duty belongs to the IaaS provider?

explanations.A: Business data policy remains customer-owned.
explanations.C: Provider infrastructure supports the VM.
explanations.D: Business access remains customer-owned.

stem: A container is hosted on a customer-managed VM. What duty remains?

choices.B: No infrastructure work of any kind

explanations.A: Packaging does not require public information.
explanations.C: Container packaging does not transfer host maintenance.
explanations.D: Facility systems belong to Microsoft.

stem: What tradeoff accompanies IaaS control?

choices.C: More guest OS and application operational responsibility

explanations.A: Workloads retain their dependencies.
explanations.C: Control includes maintenance duties.
explanations.D: That describes SaaS rather than infrastructure.

stem: What does PaaS primarily provide?

choices.A: A managed platform for customer applications
choices.B: Infrastructure with customer-managed guest operating systems

explanations.A: Customers deploy code without operating the underlying platform.
explanations.B: That describes the IaaS responsibility boundary.
explanations.C: Service use does not transfer hardware.
explanations.D: That is a SaaS example.

stem: A team wants custom web code without underlying OS administration. What model fits?

choices.B: Private cloud as a service model
choices.C: SaaS that does not support deploying this custom code

explanations.A: That retains OS administration.
explanations.B: Private classifies deployment rather than service responsibility.
explanations.C: A finished application may not meet the custom-code requirement.
explanations.D: A managed application platform matches the requirement.

stem: Which responsibility remains for a PaaS web-app customer?

explanations.A: That is provider infrastructure.
explanations.C: The provider manages the platform, not all customer behavior.
explanations.D: PaaS normally handles that layer.

stem: What can prevent a particular app from fitting a PaaS service?

choices.B: An unsupported runtime or OS-level dependency

explanations.A: PaaS can be monitored.
explanations.C: Confidentiality alone does not rule out PaaS.
explanations.D: Network use is normal for platforms.

stem: A PaaS deployment succeeds but code returns wrong results. Who investigates the code?

choices.D: No one because PaaS code cannot fail

explanations.A: Managed hosting does not fix application logic.
explanations.C: Facility cooling does not debug code.
explanations.D: Managed platforms can run faulty code.

stem: Which PaaS claim is accurate?

choices.B: Underlying platform work is reduced while customer code duties remain
choices.C: Customers must replace Azure disks physically

explanations.A: Access still needs configuration.
explanations.C: Providers maintain hardware.
explanations.D: Services have capability boundaries.

stem: Which example most clearly represents SaaS?

choices.A: A runtime for deploying custom web code
choices.D: A VM requiring guest OS management

explanations.A: That is PaaS.
explanations.C: The customer consumes ready business software.
explanations.D: That is IaaS.

stem: What does a SaaS customer generally configure?

choices.A: Users, access, and permitted application settings

explanations.A: The finished product still needs customer administration.
explanations.C: The provider maintains underlying infrastructure.
explanations.D: Hardware is provider-maintained.

stem: A charity needs standard email without writing an email app. Which model fits?

explanations.A: A blob tier is not email software.
explanations.C: That adds OS/application operations.
explanations.D: Finished software meets the stated business need.

stem: Which obligation remains in SaaS?

choices.C: Implementing the SaaS vendor's entire source code

explanations.A: Managed software does not remove these duties.
explanations.C: The vendor maintains the product.
explanations.D: The provider operates its software platform.

stem: What distinguishes SaaS from PaaS for a learner?

choices.B: SaaS supplies a finished application rather than a custom-code platform

explanations.A: It is a service model independent of deployment.
explanations.C: Managed services still run on infrastructure.
explanations.D: Customer access still needs control.

stem: An organization purchases SaaS. What should it avoid assuming?

choices.C: All data governance transfers to the vendor

explanations.A: That is expected for SaaS.
explanations.C: Customer information policies remain relevant.
explanations.D: That duty remains.

stem: What does serverless abstract for a developer?

choices.D: The existence of all physical servers

explanations.A: The provider operates the compute environment.
explanations.C: Logic and error handling remain customer duties.
explanations.D: Servers still exist.

stem: Which task naturally matches event-driven functions?

choices.B: Maintain a required custom OS kernel
choices.D: Process an image when a new upload arrives

explanations.A: That is physical maintenance.
explanations.B: Functions do not supply guest OS administration.
explanations.C: That is a SaaS requirement.
explanations.D: An upload event can trigger short processing.

stem: Which statement about Azure Functions pricing is safest?

choices.B: Billing depends on hosting plan and usage
choices.D: Every plan charges only per execution

explanations.A: Free allowances and pricing are bounded.
explanations.B: Functions supports multiple plans with different economics.
explanations.C: Functions hosting can incur costs.
explanations.D: That blanket claim is false.

stem: Why should an event handler consider idempotency?

choices.D: An event may be retried and must not duplicate harmful effects

explanations.A: Resource limits still exist.
explanations.C: Serverless still uses infrastructure.
explanations.D: Retry-safe logic supports robust processing.

stem: Who remains responsible for a function's application logic?

explanations.A: The function needs maintenance.
explanations.B: Manufacturing does not own function behavior.
explanations.C: Serverless abstracts infrastructure, not business code.
explanations.D: Facility operation does not maintain customer logic.

stem: What should be checked before assuming function cold-start behavior?

choices.A: Only the assumption that every plan bills per execution
choices.B: The selected hosting plan and configuration
choices.C: Whether all cloud apps are identical
choices.D: Only its code's programming language regardless of plan

explanations.A: Billing and startup behavior differ among plans.
explanations.B: Plans differ in execution and scaling characteristics.
explanations.C: Applications and plans differ.
explanations.D: Hosting behavior also depends on the selected plan.

stem: A custom website needs supported runtime hosting and minimal OS work. What is a reasoned choice?

choices.A: Evaluate a managed PaaS web platform
choices.C: Choose SaaS email as the website host
choices.D: Choose an OS-customized VM without checking need

explanations.A: It fits custom code with managed OS operation.
explanations.C: Email software is not a custom-code platform.
explanations.D: That adds maintenance unnecessarily.

stem: A design requires an unsupported kernel driver. What should change?

choices.A: Reassess hosting for required OS control
choices.C: Assume every managed platform supports it

explanations.A: A VM may satisfy controls unavailable in managed hosting.
explanations.B: That does not address OS compatibility.
explanations.C: Capability boundaries must be checked.
explanations.D: Renaming does not add capabilities.

stem: Which dimensions should guide service-model selection?

choices.B: Only whether the service uses a private IP
choices.C: Only the lowest advertised price without checking compatibility
choices.D: Required control, functionality, and maintenance burden

explanations.A: Popularity does not establish fit.
explanations.B: Networking alone does not select responsibility boundaries.
explanations.C: An incompatible platform cannot satisfy the requirement.
explanations.D: The choice must fit workload requirements.

stem: A team packages a container. Has it fully selected its service model?

choices.A: No, containers cannot run in Azure
choices.B: No, the hosting service still determines operational responsibilities
choices.D: Yes, every container requires customer-owned hardware

explanations.A: Azure supports container services.
explanations.B: Packaging and hosting are separate choices.
explanations.C: Containers are not inherently finished software.
explanations.D: Managed container hosting exists.

stem: Two hosting approaches both fit basic functionality. What can decide between them?

choices.B: Operational control and acceptable maintenance effort
choices.C: Whether both are called cloud services

explanations.A: Security remains necessary.
explanations.C: The generic label does not distinguish maintenance duties.
explanations.D: No general hosting model does that.

stem: What makes a service-model recommendation defensible?

choices.A: Map workload requirements to capability and remaining duties
choices.B: Claim the model removes all responsibility
choices.C: Select solely by public or private IP
choices.D: Use the same model for every workload

explanations.A: A reasoned choice explains both fit and obligations.
explanations.C: Networking does not define service responsibility.
explanations.D: Different requirements can need different services.
